meta.title: Quick fix for function no return value, `Ok()` out of function body
meta.fix_ref: rust-lang/rust-analyzer#17763 (fix: Insert a tail `Ok(())` for expr block instead of wrapping with `Ok`)
meta.build_notes: GitHub release assets rust-analyzer-aarch64-apple-darwin.gz of the weekly tags 2024-07-29 and 2024-08-05; git tag --contains puts the fix first in 2024-08-05. The sysroot is the local rustup toolchain (rustc 1.98.1).
meta.notes: The type-mismatch fix for a unit body in a function returning Result wrapped the whole body expression in Ok(...), including the braces of the function body, producing 'fn foo() -> Result<()> Ok({})'.

settings_note: The issue names no settings; the session keeps checkOnSave off (native analysis only).

files.source: issue body, 'code snippet to reproduce' block

files.note: a binary crate around the snippet (package name, version, edition 2021)

repro.steps: Open src/main.rs. The empty body of 'fn foo() -> Result<()> {}' (line 2, character 23) is reported (type mismatch, expected Result<()>, found ()). Apply its quick fix (wrap in Ok / insert Ok(())). Reported: 'fn foo() -> Result<()> Ok({})', which does not parse; expected '{ Ok(()) }'. Probe: the edited text must have no parse error that the original did not have.
